html:
SMTO-GWT-0035 — SMTO has no working way to reach the chosen computer

GUID: c6b4654d-a58a-4ede-8ba5-abb8aba9322c
Slug: gateway-endpoint-missing
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find a working connection to the computer this work should run on. It may not be set up, may be switched off in SMTO, or, for a computer that connects to SMTO itself, may not be connected right now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways. Find the computer and make sure its switch is On. If it isn't listed, select Add Gateway and enter its Host and Port. SMTO can only send work to a computer that is listed and switched on, and schedules need at least one switched-on Gateway.
  2. Select Check connection for that computer. If it is marked Outbound, start the Gateway program on that computer so it connects back to SMTO. A computer that connects to SMTO itself can only receive work while it is connected.
  3. Before sending again, look at the results of any earlier Task on that computer to see whether it already ran. Losing the connection doesn't prove that earlier work there didn't happen.

What success looks like

  • The computer shows Connected in the Gateways list, and your Task or schedule starts or saves without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up that Gateway. Don't point a saved schedule or running Task at a different computer as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway routing found no usable execution route for the intended target: no Gateway URL/host or node is configured, no enabled default Gateway exists, the captured Gateway record disappeared, or an outbound Gateway has no connected session.

What this means

  • Routing lacks the required configured host, node, default or usable endpoint, the captured record disappeared, or an outbound route has no connected session. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Routing lacks the required configured host, node, default or usable endpoint, the captured record disappeared, or an outbound route has no connected session.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify which prerequisite is missing in the route detail: registered host, default selection, node, supported URL or outbound session.

How to fix it

  • In Settings › Setup › Gateways, confirm the intended Gateway record exists, is enabled and has a host/port or node; for config-seeded nodes check AOR_DEFAULT_NODE, AOR_GATEWAY_URL and the per-node endpoint map. For an outbound Gateway, restart it on its host so its hello (including a node) re-establishes the session. Before dispatching new work, check whether earlier work on that target already ran.
  • Complete the missing target registration or default selection; reconnect the configured peer for an outbound session failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended target resolves to its verified transport and is available before new work is dispatched.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
